newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian telecoms to raise prices by 40 percent.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian telecoms to raise prices by 40 percent.

text.p: The Bulgarian Telecommunications Company (BTC), preparing for privatisation next year, plans to raise rates by 40 percent to compensate for losses from the fall in the lev, BTC director Mihail Danov said on Monday.
He said Bulgaria still had the lowest telephone rates in Europe and the increase would not cover upgrading costs.

"We will propose to the cabinet to increase telephone rates by 40 percent. The increase will compensate for losses of 25 million lev made by the BTC over the past two weeks," Danov told a news conference.
Panic buying of dollars has pushed the lev down to 355 to the dollar on Monday from 255 two weeks ago.
In a bid to raise desperately needed cash, the government has offered 25 percent of the BTC for privatisation, hoping to attract leading telecommunication companies next year.
Jointly with the World Bank, Bulgaria's privatisation agency is preparing an international tender for consultancy firms with experience in telecommunications.
The BTC is expected to post an eight billion lev 1996 pre-tax profit said Danov, with expected revenue by year-end estimated at 35 billion levs.
"Telecommunications are one of the few areas showing growth this year. BTC posted growth of 22 percent in real terms for 1996 compared to last year," said Danov.

The head of the Post and Telecommunications Committee, Lyubomir Kolarov, told the same news conference Bulgaria was expected to launch three new optic telephone links with neighbouring countries by year-end.
"With these links Bulgaria will be able to provide high quality phone links between the Middle East, Western Europe and the Baltics," said Kolarov.

The first optic link will be between the Bulgarian Danube River port of Rousse and the Romanian town of Giurgiu, which would enable the BTC to expand the telephone traffic to the Baltic countries, said Kolarov.
The other optic cable link between the southern Bulgarian town of Svilengrad and the Turkish town of Ohrid would expand the telephone traffic from the Middle East, said Kolarov.
The third link is to be launched between the eastern town of Kyustendil and Skopje, the capital of the former Yugoslav republic of Macedonia.
"We will start negotiatiations with international operators for rerouting the telephone traffic via the new optic links and expect to boost our revenue from fees," said Kolarov.
Bulgaria already launched an optic telephone link between Sofia and the Yugoslav town of Nish four months ago to ease traffic to western Europe via Belgrade and with Asia via Sofia.
